findings.evidence: `Submodule.mem_of_localization_maximal`, the lemma used at line 92, is itself stated for abstract families: `mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/LocalProperties/Submodule.lean:28-38` binds `(Rₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal R) [P.IsMaximal], Type*) … [IsLocalization.AtPrime (Rₚ P) P]` and `(Mₚ …)`. `IsDomain`/`IsFractionRing` enter only via `Localization.subalgebra`, which requires `[IsFractionRing A K]` and `S ≤ A⁰` (`mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/AsSubring.lean:29-33,83`). The repo's own curve code works with abstract subrings of `F` (`TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/AffineModel/Place.lean:123`: `{B} [CommRing B] [Algebra B F] [IsFractionRing B F]`), and 36 files use `IsLocalization.AtPrime`-style local rings.
findings.fix: State it over a family, as Mathlib does: `variable (Aₚ : ∀ (P : Ideal A) [P.IsMaximal], Type*)` with `[CommRing (Aₚ P)] [Algebra A (Aₚ P)] [IsLocalization.AtPrime (Aₚ P) P] [Algebra R (Aₚ P)] [Algebra (Aₚ P) F]` and the three towers, concluding `ω ∈ (map R R A F).range ↔ ∀ P [P.IsMaximal], ω ∈ ((map R R (Aₚ P) F).restrictScalars A).range`, with no `IsDomain`/`IsFractionRing`. The existing proof goes through verbatim (`range_kaehler_map_localization` is already stated for abstract `B`); the current statement is then the instantiation `Aₚ P := Localization.subalgebra F P.primeCompl P.primeCompl_le_nonZeroDivisors`.
findings.issue: `mem_range_kaehler_map_fractionRing_iff` (and the right-hand side of `existsUnique_kaehler_preimage_iff`, line 102) fixes the local ring to `let B := Localization.subalgebra F P.primeCompl _`. The mathematical content needs only an abstract localization of `A` at `P.primeCompl` sitting inside `F`; the `[IsDomain A]`/`[IsFractionRing A F]` hypotheses (line 72) exist solely to construct that one model, so the criterion as stated cannot be applied to local rings presented as `IsLocalization.AtPrime` (how they arrive in this repo) without transport.

findings.evidence: Lines 107-110 prove injectivity via `IsLocalizedModule.injective_iff_isRegular` (`mathlib/Mathlib/Algebra/Module/LocalizedModule/Basic.lean:552`), which only needs `IsLocalizedModule S (map R R A B)` — available for every `[IsLocalization S B]` by the instance `KaehlerDifferential.isLocalizedModule_map` (`mathlib/Mathlib/RingTheory/Etale/Kaehler.lean:63`), not just for `S = A⁰`. `hinj` is used at line 113 only in the uniqueness component.
findings.fix: Add the general lemma first, e.g. `theorem injective_kaehler_map (S : Submonoid A) [IsLocalization S B] [Module.IsTorsionFree A Ω[A⁄R]] (hS : S ≤ A⁰) : Function.Injective (map R R A B)`, and derive `existsUnique_kaehler_preimage_iff` from it plus the membership criterion (the current file's case is `S = A⁰`, `B = F`).
findings.issue: The general result — `Module.IsTorsionFree A Ω[A⁄R]` implies `Function.Injective (map R R A B)` for any localization `B` of `A` at regular elements — is proved inline as `hinj` and never stated, while the specialized `∃!` wrapper is the public API. The module docstring (line 21) advertises exactly that injectivity as a result of the file, but no user can get it; and since existence is already `mem_range_kaehler_map_fractionRing_iff`, the torsion-free hypothesis of `existsUnique_kaehler_preimage_iff` buys only uniqueness.

summary: The two maximal-ideal theorems are stated only for the hard-coded model `Localization.subalgebra F P.primeCompl`, which forces `[IsDomain A] [IsFractionRing A F]` on a statement that needs neither; and the general injectivity of `map R R A F` from torsion-freeness is proved inline instead of being the lemma from which the `∃!` form is derived.
